description:
This was orignially a larger PR, but I've shelved the larger refactoring for now.
This PR does two things:

* Add a new method `tryparse(::Type{T}, c::AbstractChar; base::Integer=10) where {T <: Integer}` which was previously missing
* Speed up parsing of chars to integer by ~4x

comments.body:
```suggestion
        codepoint - UInt8('A') + UInt8(10) # + 10 for the 10 digits
```
Given that the comment is referring to "10" and the other UInt8s around here are expressed as conversion from more semantically clear types.
TBH I find this style more clear than the style introduced in this PR
One is longer than the other, and therefore the line needs to be broken up.

`check_valid_base(base)` is already defined in this file and used by some implementations.

https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/blob/4a9de7250974a9f875f548e87d429e8df3b7d6ab/base/parse.jl#L252-L257

And it's used such that `tryparse` will throw an error if the base is invalid, unlike your definitions.

Also `tryparse_internal` uses `throw(ArgumentError(LazyString(...)))`, which looks a bit like a trick to do the same kind of thing as your `noinline` functions. Do you know which should be preferred?

Suggestion: I've updated my PR to use the parse_char method you defined (renamed as tryparse_internal), but without the `@noinline` methods. Maybe we join forces and edit + merge that version? https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/pull/47617

Consider allowing `parse(Float64, '1')` to work.

I did it like this in my PR:

https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/blob/48bd70bcd8537043179440779b7b426282ff466d/base/parse.jl#L54-L68
Should this use the `codepoint(c)` method rather than converting straight to UInt8?

It seems strange to me to have an `@inline`d method that throws. We normally want to keep error paths outlined. Even when using `LazyString`, having it outlined is better.
There is something to be said for unifying the base checking throughout the file, i.e. have all paths use the outlined `_invalid_base` function.
FYI This is equivalent to a `::T` return type annotation.

In general, I try to avoid second guessing the compiler on inlining heuristics unless I'm very familiar with the code and all its callsites and/or I've measured performance differences that confirm that I know better than the compiler.

This inlining choice seems accurate to me so I'm willing to proceed with the annotation if you think it helps performance.
